facts.text: Ark was named for Henry Stuart, Duke of Gloucester, the third son of King Charles I, a nod to Virginia’s colonial heritage.
Ark sits 85 feet above sea level in the Tidewater plain, close to the York River and Chesapeake Bay.
Ark lies roughly three miles west‑northwest of Gloucester Courthouse, reached by Route 17 and State Route 14.
The area enjoys a humid subtropical climate, averaging 60 °F year‑round, with about 47 inches of rain and frequent summer thunderstorms.
In the mid‑17th century, settlers in Ark received tobacco land grants under the headright system, fueling Virginia’s Tidewater economy.
After the 1865 emancipation, Ark’s plantation system collapsed, prompting formerly enslaved workers to seek land ownership and independence.
